questions.title: Pearson goodness-of-fit for a fully specified multinomial null
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation in categorical inference. Let N=(N_1,...,N_k) be the category counts from n independent draws under a fully specified categorical null p=(p_1,...,p_k), where fixed k>=2, every p_j>0, and sum_j p_j=1. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of Pearson's statistic Q_n=sum_j (N_j-n p_j)^2/(n p_j), its multinomial-CLT and projection argument, and the null limit Q_n => chi-square_{k-1}. Explain why the covariance is singular, why the limiting quadratic form has rank k-1, why no parameter-estimation degrees-of-freedom correction appears here, and why the chi-square p-value is asymptotic rather than an exact finite-sample claim. The required model-authored artifact is est_multinomial_pearson_gof and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. Exploratory computation may diagnose algebra or implementation. A separate frozen confirmatory assessment uses independently generated multinomial counts in predeclared null settings whose expected cell counts are comfortably above the usual small-cell warning, checks exact statistic and category-permutation identities, and assesses null rejection calibration and the first two chi-square moments with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

request_fields.name: observed_counts
request_fields.meaning: Observed category counts N_1,...,N_k from one categorical sample.
request_fields.shape: length k with k>=2; every entry is nonnegative and the total n is positive
request_fields.indexing: entry j is paired with null_probabilities[j]
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonintegers, negative counts, fewer than two categories, and zero total count.

request_fields.name: null_probabilities
request_fields.meaning: The fully specified categorical null probabilities p_1,...,p_k, fixed independently of the observed counts.
request_fields.shape: length k equal to observed_counts; every entry is finite and strictly positive; the sum differs from one by at most 1e-12
request_fields.indexing: entry j is paired with observed_counts[j]
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, nonpositive probabilities, unequal lengths, and sums outside the stated tolerance; do not renormalize an invalid request.

response_fields.name: n_categories
response_fields.meaning: The number k of categories in the request.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be an integer at least two.

response_fields.name: expected_counts
response_fields.meaning: Expected category counts under the fully specified null.
response_fields.indexing: entry j corresponds to category j
response_fields.edge_cases: Every entry must be finite and strictly positive.

response_fields.name: pearson_contributions
response_fields.indexing: entry j corresponds to category j
response_fields.edge_cases: Every entry must be finite and nonnegative.

response_fields.name: degrees_of_freedom
response_fields.meaning: The asymptotic chi-square degrees of freedom for this fully specified null.
response_fields.normalization: n_categories-1; no parameters are estimated from observed_counts.

response_fields.name: asymptotic_p_value
response_fields.meaning: The upper-tail probability of pearson_statistic under the declared chi-square approximation.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be finite and lie in [0,1].

invariants.meaning: Expected counts equal n times the supplied probabilities, each contribution has the declared Pearson formula, the statistic is their sum, degrees_of_freedom equals k-1, and the p-value is the corresponding chi-square upper tail.

Applying the same category permutation to observed_counts and null_probabilities permutes expected_counts and pearson_contributions while preserving sample_size, pearson_statistic, degrees_of_freedom, and asymptotic_p_value.
Whenever every n*null_probabilities[j] is an integer and observed_counts equals that expected-count vector, every contribution and pearson_statistic is zero and asymptotic_p_value is one.

empirical_claims.meaning: The frozen confirmatory assessment draws independent multinomial counts from predeclared fully specified nulls with comfortably non-small expected cells and assesses rejection at alpha=0.05 plus the chi-square mean and variance, all with Monte Carlo uncertainty; these are empirical support for an asymptotic result, not proof or an exact finite-sample guarantee.

Every confirmatory call supplies the exact predeclared counts and null probabilities and separately verifies expected counts, category contributions, their sum, k-1 degrees of freedom, upper-tail p-value, category-permutation behavior, and valid output domains before aggregating calibration behavior.
